what_it_does: When engineers design radio-frequency (RF) circuits — the kind in your phone's wireless chip — they need to simulate how the circuit behaves under repeating, wave-like electrical signals. The standard simulation method, called harmonic balance, involves solving a large system of equations repeatedly through a process called Newton iterations, where each iteration refines an approximate answer. This paper proposes new 'preconditioners' — mathematical tricks that reshape the equations so they become much faster to solve without needing as many rounds of refinement. The work also introduces a way to automatically pick the right preconditioner for a given circuit by measuring how nonlinear (i.e., how far from a simple straight-line relationship) the circuit's behavior is.
